What makes a retail business rise above the rest? A well-oiled operation that keeps shelves stocked, prices competitive and customers coming back time and time again. But behind the scenes, it comes down to one crucial piece of the puzzle: the procurement process. Many might simplify procurement in retail to just buying supplies, but it’s a far more strategic process, especially for multi-location retailers where it critically impacts profitability and success.


From building relationships with reliable suppliers to negotiating favorable terms, procurement is about finding quality at the best value. And when done right, it doesn’t just protect your bottom line—it drives growth. With a streamlined procurement process, retailers can enhance inventory tracking,[optimize supply chains](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/retail-supply-chain-management/) and boost profits across every location.

## What is retail procurement?


Procurement is how businesses source and acquire essential goods and services they need to function. In the world of retail, it’s the dynamic process of identifying the best suppliers, scoring the best terms and ensuring products arrive when customers need them.


Think of it this way: effective procurement ensures your[inventory levels](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/inventory-visibility/) are perfectly balanced. It means your store is stocked with items that your customers actually want, eliminating empty spaces or excess stock tying up resources.


For retailers, procurement is more than just an administrative box to be checked; it’s a direct driver of profitability and customer satisfaction. Ultimately, it ensures that your customers find exactly what they’re looking for, fostering trust and loyalty that keeps them coming back. For[retailers managing multiple locations](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/multi-location-business/) , a seamless procurement strategy is the foundation upon which growth and success in a demanding market are built.

Simplify your systems and make more informed decisions with reporting. Keep reading to hear how CBD Kratom keeps innovating across 62 stores with Lightspeed.


## Types of procurement in retail


[Procurement in retail](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/retail-procurement-management-tips-for-your-store/) isn’t one-size-fits-all, though. It breaks down into distinct categories, each serving a specific purpose to keep operations running, inventory stocked and costs in check.


### Direct retail procurement


When it comes to procurement for retail, the first thought that probably comes to mind is buying inventory to sell it to consumers. That’s direct retail procurement; picture all the SKUs in a store—they were directly procured.


### Indirect retail procurement


That means indirect retail procurement refers to whatever is purchased by a retailer but will never be sold to a customer. This can be store supplies, fixtures, technology, and more.


### Goods vs. services retail procurement


You can procure the previously mentioned goods for your retail store, as well as services. Your services might include maintenance, cleaning, and security, for example.


### Strategic retail procurement


While it’s standard to invest in goods and services for your store, it’s optional—yet highly advised—that you take a strategic approach. Think about how your inventory can help you avoid overstock and stockouts. Think about how your service providers can help you elevate the store experience and even the work experience for your teams. Consider how investing in snacks and beverages for employees can help them manage their energy levels throughout the day. Think about how your technology purchases can reduce customer wait times and help you drive more sales.

**Direct procurement** Securing goods directly tied to what the business sells. Products for resale, raw materials, finished goods; grocery store buying produce, clothing store sourcing apparel. Directly affects sales and customer satisfaction; timing and accuracy are crucial.

Overarching strategy; elevates procurement beyond fulfilling immediate needs to creating a competitive advantage.


## The procurement process in retail


### Step 1: Needs identification


Everything starts with knowing exactly what your business needs. Retailers look at customer demand, stock levels and operational priorities to figure out what products or services to procure. Tools like market analysis and sales forecasting help you[predict demand](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/inventory-forecasting/) and guide well-informed purchasing choices.


### Step 2: Supplier research and selection


Next, you should be focusing on the reliability and quality of your supplier. Retailers research potential vendors, evaluate their pricing and delivery timelines, and prioritize partners with proven track records. It’s also smart to diversify your sourcing. Relying on just one supplier can leave you vulnerable to delays or shortages, so spreading out risk keeps your supply chain stronger.


Read more on how to[find the best manufacturer or supplier](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/finding-a-manufacturer-or-supplier/) for your business.


### Step 3: Purchase requisition


Once you know what you need and who you’ll source it from, the next step is internal approval. A purchase requisition lists what’s being requested and ensures it fits within your budget and stock plan. It’s a straightforward but essential step to make sure every purchase supports your bottom line.


### Step 4: Order placement


After approvals, it’s time to place your order.[A purchase order](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/purchase-orders/) is sent to the supplier, confirming quantities, delivery dates and terms. Many businesses now use electronic systems, like Lightspeed’s[Retail POS](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/pos/retail/) to simplify this—making it easier to track orders, avoid errors and keep everything moving efficiently.


### Step 5: Receiving and inspection


Your order’s arrived, but the process isn’t over just yet. Receiving and inspection are crucial checkpoints that ensure everything’s right as rain.


Retailers carefully inspect deliveries to make sure everything matches the order. Quality, quantities and accuracy are checked, and any issues are addressed directly with the supplier. This step prevents problems like stockouts,[excess inventory](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/what-is-excess-inventory/) or disappointing customers with faulty products.


### Step 6: Payment and recordkeeping


The procurement journey wraps up with payment and recordkeeping. This step is all about matching invoices with purchase orders, processing payments and keeping meticulous records for future reference. Using tools like[Lightspeed Payments](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/pos/retail/payments/) makes transactions quicker and more accurate, ensuring payments are processed smoothly without disrupting your workflow. Clear, organized records make everything easier; when your documentation is easy to follow, you’re in a stronger position to make smarter decisions that help your business grow.


## Advantages of effective procurement in retail


Advantage Description


Cost saving Effective procurement controls costs by securing bulk discounts, better payment terms, and reduced storage expenses. It also prevents costly mistakes like[overstocking](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/manage-surplus-overstock-inventory/) , freeing up cash flow for growth.


Inventory optimization[Just-in-time inventory](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/just-in-time-inventory-management/) ensures stock arrives when needed, cutting storage costs and boosting turnover rates. Aligning inventory with demand keeps your business efficient and responsive.


Improved supplier relationships Strong supplier relationships mean consistency, faster problem-solving and better terms. Collaboration with trusted partners leads to creative solutions during disruptions and high-demand periods.


Operational efficiency A streamlined procurement process eliminates delays and confusion, allowing your team to focus on growth-driving activities like boosting sales and enhancing customer service.


Risk mitigation Diversifying suppliers and planning ahead minimizes risks from disruptions, ensuring business continuity when it matters most.


## Procurement vs. purchasing in retail


While procurement and purchasing both refer to obtaining resources, these terms aren’t actually interchangeable in retail. Use the term procurement when you’re referring to something you’re buying as a long-term, strategic investment to demonstrate. Understanding retail procurement is long-term, unsurprisingly, purchasing refers to short-term, transactional expenditures.


## Retail procurement best practices


Here are some actionable considerations to manage costs, efficiency, and the quality of your relationships with suppliers:


### Building and maintaining strong supplier relationships


Relationships are the backbone of procurement for retail. It’s important to maintain respectful, transparent, and professional relationships with your suppliers. When you work as a team, you can identify more mutual opportunities for growth and have an easier time navigating and resolving challenges.


### Leverage technology (procurement software, automation tools)


Incorporate tech into your retail procurement strategy. Use procurement software to simplify and speed up the buying process, and use automation tools to save additional time (such as submitting one-click reorders).


### Forecasting demand to prevent stockouts


Use demand forecasting to make it far more likely that you’ll carry enough of a popular SKU or category in your stores. It’s important to avoid stockouts; they can damage the perception of your business, lead to hiccups in service, frustrate your customers, and inspire customers to shop elsewhere.


### Standardizing processes and documentation


It pays to invest the time and effort to get organized upfront. When you standardize your processes and documentation, it makes it faster and easier to procure in the future. It also makes it easier to get new team members up to speed faster.


### Using data-driven decision-making


Let’s say you’re procuring inventory—use data to make ever better decisions. Study what sold best months ago or last year, what could have sold better, trending colors or categories and other data points to help inform future buys.


### Risk management in procurement


Diversify your suppliers, and stay informed about what you procure from where. Things change. You might need backup suppliers for key considerations, and it’s also important to diversify to spread out risk. For instance, if the vast majority of your inventory comes from just one to three suppliers, even a little supply chain disruption could spell big trouble for your business.


## Changes in retail procurement


Procurement for retail tends to exist in a state of flux. Here are some of the most common variables that shake things up:


### Disruptions in supply chain


Supply chain disruptions may be caused by geopolitical events and incidents, severe weather that impacts shipping or air freight, sourcing disruptions or shortages, manufacturing facility issues, and more.


### Fluctuations in price


Vendors’ prices can change when key components, ingredients, materials, or manufacturing needs experience price volatility.


### Managing vendor relationships


Sometimes it will be necessary to part ways with vendors. Maybe a vendor will take an extended pause or wind down their business. Or perhaps they’ll no longer maintain great communication or maybe something could occur that could cause trust to be broken. Whatever the cause, there can be a myriad of reasons why you might stop or temporarily pause working with a specific supplier.


### Quality control issues


If you start experiencing repeat quality-control issues, it could be time to replace that vendor (if they’re not able to course correct).


### Seasonal demand variations


Your orders will naturally change throughout the year to reflect changes in seasonality. For instance, for a sporting goods store, you might sell swimming accessories and ice skates throughout the year for indoor and outdoor use, but you’d probably stock fewer swim accessories in winter and fewer ice skates in the warmer months.


### Retail assortment complexity


As you gauge market trends, sales, shifts in consumer behavior, and other variables, you’ll strategically adjust the categories, quantities, colors, and materials you carry over time.


## Retail procurement optimization strategies


On the topic of strategy, it’s important to take care as you choose the best retail procurement optimization approaches for your stores. Develop a few essential strategies for the following considerations: forecasting demand, minimizing risk, reducing costs, and meeting specific ethical and social good considerations (such as Fair Trade and sustainability).


## Impact of procurement on retail operations


Procurement in retail industry businesses will have an impact on your margins, profitability,[retail operations](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/retail-operations/) , customer service—and even your stores’ reputations. It’s important to be strategic about all of your procurement decisions to balance considerations such as value and cost-saving with offering a desirable assortment and supporting vendors you can trust.


## Bottom line


Procurement is more than buying up the right products—it’s the backbone of running a successful retail operation. It’s where supplier relationships,[inventory planning](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/inventory-management-techniques/) and cost control come together. When done right, it cuts unnecessary expenses, keeps stock levels accurate and ensures you’re always ready to provide the best[customer experience](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/blog/4-ways-to-create-a-strong-retail-customer-experience/) you can.

## FAQs on retail procurement


### What are the challenges of procurement in retail?


Procurement in retail industry businesses comes with its fair share of challenges. Supply chain disruptions can throw off delivery schedules, while unpredictable demand makes it harder to keep shelves stocked without overordering. Relying on a single supplier adds risk—any delays or quality issues can leave you scrambling—yet juggling multiple suppliers often means more complexity. For retailers with multiple locations, staying on top of delivery timelines and maintaining product quality takes careful planning.


### How is strategic procurement different from regular procurement?


Instead of just buying what you need, strategic procurement is about creating long-term value. It prioritizes building strong supplier relationships, negotiating better terms and ensuring procurement aligns with broader business goals. Regular procurement is more straightforward, focusing mainly on the immediate purchase of goods or services. Strategic procurement goes deeper—it improves reliability, streamlines operations and delivers consistency across all locations.


### What are the benefits of strategic procurement in retail?


Approaching procurement strategically can increase profits, streamline operations, improve inventory, reduce lags in service or delays in receiving goods, and more.


### What role does forecasting play in retail procurement?


Forecasting helps you predict true demand with greater accuracy so you can reduce the odds of ending up with stockouts or overstock.


### What are the future trends in retail procurement?


Retail procurement is changing with the introduction of AI-powered tools (such as for deeper insights or predictions pertaining to risk management), tech platforms designed for retailer-supplier collaboration, and the use of blockchains to maintain transparent supply chains (such as to verify ethical sourcing and sustainability).
